Tables M.T1 and M.T2 are remarkably similar, with the main restriction coming down to a portion of the southern tip of the county just outside the 20-mile buffer zone for the Yellowstone River. As with Rosebud county, the terrain shifts moving south, leading to more changes in elevation and therefore potential restriction due to slope. The only other criterion that presents a barrier to siting any of these technologies is areas of open water, which mostly just excludes the Yellowstone itself, along with some tributaries spread throughout the county. Treasure County does not appear to contain any regions with meaningful geological hazards or floodplains, and while no areas indicate a population density exceeding the 500 ppsm threshold, further analysis is required to pinpoint existing population centers that may be desirable to avoid. 37 Table M.T1: Data Package for Large Light Water Reactor for Treasure Montana Large LWR (e.g., AP1000)
